issues.description: Resolver.resolve() postcondition silently weakened; returned requirements may no longer be fully prepared.
issues.detail: The resolver used to guarantee every requirement had prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False. That guarantee is removed and the obligation shifted to callers without documenting the new contract. Any caller (third-party, plugin, future command like lock) inheriting the old assumption gets a half-prepared state. Document the new postcondition on resolve() and on RequirementSet.

issues.description: Identical prepare_linked_requirements_more call copy-pasted into three commands instead of a shared helper.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each grew the same line, creating an implicit, unenforced precondition on every consumer of resolve(). A fourth command (e.g. lock) will forget. Push it back into resolve() behind a flag (dry_run=True) or extract one helper so the contract is enforced in one place.

issues.description: set_dist caches a metadata-only distribution that is never invalidated after the full download lands.
issues.detail: _fetch_metadata_only stores a metadata_dist in self._distribution. After prepare_linked_requirements_more performs the real download, get_dist() still returns the cached metadata-only dist. If the two diverge (RECORD, file list, install paths) callers get silently wrong behavior. Invalidate _distribution on full prep, or document that the cache wins and assert equivalence.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist introduced without preconditions, postconditions, or invariants documented.
issues.detail: set_dist accepts any BaseDistribution with no docstring, no constraints on when calling is valid, and no statement of what callers may assume afterward. For a mutable cache touched by resolver, preparer, and installer, the spec is the contract. At minimum, document that it stores a metadata-only view, may be superseded, and is not thread-safe.

issues.description: download_info now has two producers with no documented precedence, and the metadata path may use an unset source_dir.
issues.detail: direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) populates download_info in _fetch_metadata_only when None, but in dry-run source_dir may be unset, especially for VCS URLs. Two producers (metadata path and full-download path) may also yield subtly different hashes/archive_info that pip lock and --report consumers depend on. Document precedence and test dry-run with VCS + --report.

issues.description: No test coverage in the diff for the headline behavior change.
issues.detail: The point of the patch is that --dry-run no longer downloads full wheels. That is a one-line assertion in a functional test: run --dry-run against a wheel with PEP-658 metadata and assert the wheel bytes were not fetched. The diff ships zero tests. Add a test that fails without the patch and passes with it.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the performance intent (defer full preparation out of resolve() so --dry-run and lock/--report can use metadata-only fetches) is sound, but the execution weakens contracts without writing them down. Resolver.resolve()'s postcondition is silently relaxed and the replacement step is copy-pasted across three commands instead of consolidated, creating an unenforced precondition future callers will forget. The new set_dist/get_dist cache has no invalidation when the real download lands — a correctness landmine — and download_info now has two producers with no documented precedence. The headline behavior also ships with no visible test. NEEDS-WORK: document the new contracts, invalidate the metadata-only dist on full prep, consolidate the call site, and add a dry-run regression test.
